content: A happy life is one which is in accordance with its own nature.
author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Tranquillitate Animi (On Tranquility of Mind)
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Water is the softest thing on earth, yet it carves through solid granite. It doesn't fight obstacles; it yields, flows around them, and quietly finds its way to its natural level.

Seneca understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. When we force outcomes with brute willpower and anxiety, we exhaust ourselves and create unnecessary resistance. Aligning with nature means trusting the timing of things and moving with steady, patient persistence.
reflectionPrompt: What lesson in endurance or renewal can you draw from the natural world today?
